record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For random sub-unitary channels, prove maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), at least at p = 2, or determine whether these channels yield additional counterexamples to multiplicativity.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, channels with Kraus operators of the form (21) have interesting properties that makes them worth further study.
Problem 15. Can one prove (24) for random sub-unitary channels, at least for p = 2. If not, do these channels provide additional counter-example?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}^n)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}^m)$. Any such channel admits a Kraus representation $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{k=1}^{K} A_k \rho A_k^*$ with $\sum_k A_k^* A_k = I_n$. For $p\ge 1$, the maximal output $p$-norm of $\Phi$ is
$$\nu_p(\Phi)\ :=\ \sup_{\rho}\ \|\Phi(\rho)\|_p,$$
where the supremum is over density matrices $\rho$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$.

A random sub-unitary channel is constructed as follows. Fix integers $n,K\ge 1$ with $K\le n^2$. Sample $K$ independent $n\times n$ matrices $\{A_k\}_{k=1}^K$ whose entries are i.i.d.\ complex Gaussians (suitably normalized), and rescale so that $\sum_{k=1}^K A_k^* A_k = I_n$ (equivalently, take Kraus operators of "sub-unitary" form, namely properly normalized truncations of Haar-random unitaries, so that each $A_k$ is, up to scaling, a contraction). The resulting channel $\Phi$ is called a random sub-unitary channel.

Problem. Let $\Phi$ and $\Omega$ be independent random sub-unitary channels. Prove that with probability one (or in expectation, in the appropriate scaling regime),
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes \Omega)\ =\ \nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega),$$
at least in the case $p=2$. If this multiplicativity fails, exhibit random sub-unitary channels that provide explicit counterexamples to multiplicativity of the maximal output $p$-norm.
artifact.status_search_result: General multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm is known to fail for all p>1 (Hayden–Winter and follow-ups), and random quantum channels are known to provide violations for p>2. For p=2 some weak multiplicativity results for random channels exist (e.g., Montanaro and Collins–Nechita), but a definitive proof or disproof of multiplicativity at p=2 specifically for the random sub-unitary class described does not appear in the located literature, so the status of this specific question is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to the Maximal p-Norm Multiplicativity Conjecture for all p > 1
status_evidence.snippet: For all p>1 there exist quantum channels with non-multiplicative maximal output p-norms.
status_evidence.claim: Multiplicativity fails in general for all p>1, but the construction does not directly resolve the random sub-unitary case at p=2.

status_evidence.title: Weak Multiplicativity for Random Quantum Channels
status_evidence.snippet: A weaker variant of multiplicativity holds for random quantum channels.
status_evidence.claim: Random channels satisfy weak multiplicativity but the strong equality at p=2 for sub-unitary channels is not established.

status_evidence.title: The maximum output p-norm of quantum channels is not multiplicative for any p>2
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to multiplicativity for any p>2 using random constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Random constructions yield counterexamples for p>2, leaving p=2 distinguished.
